subject: Temporary traffic hold with auto-pin & telemetry watch - AcmeCloud launch
messages:
From: Luke Harper <luke.harper@acmecloud.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary traffic hold + auto-pin escape hatch for Monday launch

Connor —

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call yesterday. We’re going live with the AcmeCloud assistant on Monday and have a slightly unusual ask from our platform team: can Redwood grant a short-lived exception to allow an automatic traffic hold with an auto-pin fallback if the canary shows an immediate regression?

Concretely:
- We want a canary (5% traffic) for 2 hours.
- If 5xx or latency P99 breaches our threshold (5xx > 1% OR P99 > 1.6s) for a rolling 10m window, we want the canary traffic to be held and requests routed to a pinned stable model version automatically.
- If pinned version is not healthy, fall back to the global stable variant.

Attached is our planned canary runbook and telemetry baseline. We understand this is an SLO carveout and are happy to sign a temporary addendum. Need to know what guardrails RedWood needs (telemetry hooks, audit logs, TTL on the exception).

Can you advise and, if possible, route to the right team for approval? We’re hoping to enable this at 08:00 PDT Monday.

— Luke
Luke Harper
Platform Lead, AcmeCloud

Attachments: acme_canary_plan.pdf (22KB), telemetry-baseline.csv (12KB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Luke Harper <luke.harper@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aaron Mills <aaron.mills@acmecloud.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary traffic hold + auto-pin escape hatch for Monday launch

Luke —

Thanks for the clear runbook. We can support the flow you describe but will need an exception approved for the SLO guardrails and a short operational checklist. Proposed Redwood-side controls: 

1) Auto-pin policy: when the canary breach condition (5xx > 1% OR P99 > 1.6s for 10m rolling) is met, the platform will pin traffic for the canary cohort to the last-known-stable model binary (pinned-version tag). Pin is timeboxed to a configurable TTL (default 6h) and will require manual extension to persist beyond that TTL.

2) Auto-swap fallback chain: pinned-version -> global-stable-1 -> global-stable-2. If the pinned-version health check fails at evaluation interval (1 min), we auto-swap to the next stable.

3) Telemetry hooks: we will enable live trace streaming to the AcmeCloud telemetry workspace and create a dedicated alert in Redwood Observability for the rolling breach. We will also capture an audit trail (who/what triggered the pin, timestamps).

4) Safety gates: a temporary "traffic hold" flag will suspend additional canary rollout; traffic is held at current rate until human confirmation or TTL expiry. We need a named approver on Acme’s side (for emergency rollback) and to assign Redwood on-call to the window.

Risk notes from infra: pinning preserves model binary but does not automatically restore cached KV state; some user sessions may see higher latency on first request post-swap. Karthik — can you confirm whether we need an explicit KV flush step?

Next steps: if this outline looks good I’ll prepare the exception request doc for legal & SRE sign-off (DocuSign link + brief addendum). Also please share the approver name for the window.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Aug 2027 14:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary traffic hold + auto-pin escape hatch for Monday launch

Connor —

Quick tech review & recommendations:

- Thresholds: 5xx>1% OR P99>1.6s (10m rolling) are reasonable for an external canary. Recommend adding a second-signal: increased model-side token retry rate > 0.8% to avoid routing on transient upstream issues.

- KV cache: pinning the model version does not roll the KV cache forward/backwards. For Acme’s workload (session-heavy), I recommend a soft KV invalidate on pin (not full flush) to avoid user-visible spikes; this can be implemented by tagging new sessions served by pinned-version to rebuild cache gradually.

- Health checks: we should run a post-pin synthetic (10 requests/min) for the first 5 minutes. If error rate remains >0.5% node-wide, escalate to manual hold.

- Implementation steps: create canary feature-flag (acme_canary_0808), add telemetry subscription, add audit log entries, add TTL=6h, and pre-create rollback runbook in the incident doc.

I’ll attach a minimal config snippet for the ops team to apply. Happy to pair on the dry-run tonight.

– Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Connor / Karthik / Luke —

I’ve reviewed the plan and the proposed technical controls. Business side sign-off: APPROVED with the following conditions — please implement before go-live and confirm in this thread: 

1) Limit: exception window to a single 24-hour period starting at the canary start time. Any extension requires formal approval from my office.
2) TTL: set default pin TTL to 6 hours; require manual extension to go beyond 6 hours.
3) Audit: enable event-level audit logging for the window and provide a summary report within 12 hours of the window ending.
4) On-call: add the infra on-call (rotation ID: infra-3) to the alert channel and ensure the runbook has a named owner.

Also: require a quick dry run tonight (simulated breach) to validate the auto-swap chain and the synthetic post-pin health check. Karthik — coordinate with Luke on timing.

Once the dry run is green, Connor please send me the finalized exception doc and I’ll route to Legal for the addendum signatures.

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
